one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08 window, within 48 hours of each other. (1) T-Mobile's Q3 2026 results on Oct 28 (~4:05pm ET release, 4:30pm call; Business Wire via finviz). Q3 is pre-guided soft on the Q2 call (~250k account adds, Core EBITDA ~+8%). Recent results days have been big in both directions: +6.1% on Apr 29 after Q1 and -10.7% on Jul 23 on Q2, then +5.7% the next day (Stock Analysis daily history). (2) The FOMC on Oct 27-28 (Fed calendar). The Fed raised rates to 3.75-4.00% on Sept 16, and the 10-year was 5.22% on Oct 8 (FRED). Polymarket's ~83.5% 'no change' (~$32.1M volume) is context only. The Oct 9 shock (-13.27%) was sector-wide: VZ fell 8.75% and T 9.81% the same day (Stock Analysis daily histories, CompaniesMarketCap). That makes it a re-pricing of the US carrier group, not an idiosyncratic overreaction, and I have no reopenable base rate for a short-term rebound (my round-1 rebound statistics came from a keyed feed and are dropped). So I stay near-symmetric around $148.58 with a +0.5% drift (median ~$149.3). For sigma: 6-month daily realized vol was 35% (Stock Analysis history, before Oct 9), which is ~10% a month. I use a mixture of 80% at sigma 10% and 20% at sigma 17% to fatten the tails for the earnings print plus FOMC.

bear.story: Competitive repricing deepens. The FCC approves SpaceX-Grain, SpaceX signs a carrier/MVNO route or prices aggressively ahead of its H1-2028 launch, and VZ/T keep pressing on price. FY2027 EPS consensus is cut ~8% to $13.28, FY2028 grows 6%, so Oct-2027 NTM EPS is ~$13.88, and the stock trades at ~8.25x (VZ's 8.23x today) = $115. Base rate: entrant shocks derate incumbents before and after launch: Orange fell -11.4%/-18.2%/-21.7% in 2010-2012 around Free Mobile's licence and launch, Bouygues -24.9% in 2011, TIM -36.6% in Iliad's 2018 launch year, and Charter is ~87% below its 2021 high amid fixed-wireless and fiber entry (CompaniesMarketCap). Rates stay above 5% on the 10-year.

base.story: TMUS delivers close to its maintained 2027 framework (Core EBITDA ~$39.5B vs the $40-41B target; AFCF ~$19.5B) and shrinks the share count to ~1,005M within the ~$30B return envelope. The SpaceX threat stays a 2028 story (CFO: service in H1 2028; the spectrum is not compatible with V1/V2 satellites), but it caps the multiple at ~10.6x NTM EPS of $14.75 = $156, below fair value ($159.6). Base rate: the year after a >10% calendar-year drop for VZ, T and TMUS (n=13) had a median price return of +1.6%, with 8 of 13 up (CompaniesMarketCap annual returns). Cheapness alone rarely re-rates a telecom within a year.

bull.story: Q3/Q4 prints and 2027 guidance confirm the $40-41B EBITDA / $19.5-20.5B AFCF framework. Estimates hold (NTM ~$15.52 with no haircut), the FCC review drags, rates ease from the Fed's September hike, and the multiple re-rates to ~12.5x, still below the ~13.6x implied before the shock (11.82x x 171.31/148.58) and inside the peer range (VOD 13.62x, TU 15.46x) = ~$195. No Deutsche Telekom offer is assumed (unverified).

comps_summary.peer_range: 10 peers (VZ, T, CMCSA, CHTR, RCI, BCE, TU, AMX, VOD, ORA), all Stock Analysis at the 2026-10-09 close, re-opened 2026-10-11. Forward P/E 2.34x (CHTR) to 15.46x (TU), median 9.95x (10.44x without CHTR). Trailing EV/EBITDA 4.58x (CMCSA) to 9.72x (TU), median 6.905x (7.13x without CHTR). Deutsche Telekom was dropped from the round-1 set because it consolidates TMUS, so its multiple is circular. Peer multiples are post-shock: VZ -8.75% and T -9.81% on Oct 9.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: P/E 11.0x vs 9.95x median (+10.6%), equal to the growth-matched AMX 10.90x / ORA 11.02x and below TMUS's current 11.82x. EV/EBITDA 7.3x vs 6.905x median (+6%), between VZ 7.13x and RCI 7.63x, below TMUS's 8.06x. FCF yield 12.0% vs VZ 12.44% / T 11.62%.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The P/E premium is not an outperformance call. It matches what the market already pays for comparable growth: AMX (3Y EPS growth 18.02%) trades at 10.90x and ORA (15.63%) at 11.02x, against TMUS's 17.03%. The peer median 3Y EPS growth is ~7.6%. The growth itself is backed by maintained company targets (2027 Core EBITDA $40-41B, about 9% above the 2026 midpoint; Sept 3 8-K 'maintains ... long-term financial framework'). I hold the premium at the growth-matched level rather than TMUS's history (year-end TTM P/E 20.8x in 2025 and 22.3x in 2023, now 15.5x, per CompaniesMarketCap) because SpaceX and cable contest exactly that growth, and part of the EPS growth comes from buybacks. On EV/EBITDA, the growth-matched peers carry no premium (AMX 5.58x, ORA 6.45x), so I use only +6%.

thesis_break_reason: $118 is ~8.2x the FY2027 consensus EPS of $14.44, below Verizon's 8.23x forward P/E, so no growth premium would be left. It is also ~15.4% FCF yield on the low end of the maintained 2027 AFCF target ($19.5B / 1,072.7M shares today = $18.18). A sustained trade there would most likely mean the 2027 framework is being abandoned (a cut to the $40-41B EBITDA / $19.5-20.5B AFCF targets), a price war, or a credible SpaceX route to scale before 2028, not ordinary volatility. The base rate supports that reading: for VZ and T over 1984-2025, a calendar-year fall of more than 20% happened in only 5-7% of years (CompaniesMarketCap), and the stock is already -26.8% YTD. My ladder still puts ~18% on a close below ~$119, because the mixture's bear leg (centred at $115) is exactly that thesis-break world.

reasoning: Start: $148.58 after a -13.27% day on Oct 9 (not -9.9%, which was an intraday figure). VZ (-8.75%) and T (-9.81%) fell the same day, so the market re-priced the whole US carrier group (six-month daily vol was ~25% for VZ and ~27% for T before the shock, vs 35% for TMUS) for SpaceX buying Grain's up-to-14MHz 800MHz spectrum (~$8B per the WSJ, via Light Reading). That deal needs FCC approval, is not compatible with SpaceX's V1/V2 satellites, and SpaceX targets service in H1 2028, after my horizon. Fundamentals on verified filings: the 2027 targets ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF) were reaffirmed as a framework on Sept 3, and the 2026 guide is $37.1-37.5B / $18.4-18.8B. I now haircut 2027 explicitly (EBITDA $39.5B, AFCF $19.5B). The horizon share count is corrected to 1,005M from 981M: the 10-Q caps 2026-27 returns at up to ~$30B including the $18.2B 2026 program, so I assumed too much buyback in round 1. Methods: P/E $162.2 (11.0x, the growth-matched AMX/ORA level), EV/EBITDA $153.8 (7.3x, +6% vs the 10-peer median), FCF yield $161.7 (12%). Fair value $159.6, down from $166.9. Base rates (my lane), now from reopenable annual returns (CompaniesMarketCap) rather than a keyed feed: (a) for VZ, T and TMUS, the year after a >10% calendar-year drop had a median price return of +1.6%, with 8 of 13 up, so cheapness is a weak 12-month catalyst. (b) Incumbents facing a well-funded entrant derate over several years, both before and in the launch year: Orange -18%/-22% in 2011/12, Bouygues -25% in 2011, TIM -37% in 2018, Charter ~-87% from its 2021 peak. Recovery came in years 2-3 (Orange +17%/+51% in 2013/14). SpaceX's launch is ~18 months out, so the horizon sits in the 'pre-launch derating' phase. (c) Annual log-volatility of US telecoms is 0.17 (VZ), 0.21 (T) and 0.22 (TMUS 2014-25), against 33% realized now (35% six-month daily). (d) Macro: the Fed hiked on Sept 16 and the 10-year rose from 4.14% to 5.22% in a year (FRED), a headwind for bond proxies. Prediction markets (Polymarket SpaceX-carrier ~$10.4k volume; Fed odds) are context only and feed no probability. Synthesis: a mixture of bear $115 (28%, sigma 0.24), base $156 (50%, sigma 0.17) and bull $195 (22%, sigma 0.19). That gives a median of ~$153 (+3%), a mean of ~$156 and log dispersion ~0.27: between the telecom annual base rate and today's elevated realized vol, and left-skewed for the entrant-shock pattern. The median sits below fair value because the base rates say re-rating takes longer than a year when the threat is still ahead. Research limits: Yahoo's chart API returned 429 and Macrotrends showed a bot challenge, so neither was used. Stooq did not connect. Long-run base rates therefore use calendar-year returns, not drawdown-dated windows. No option data was consulted.
